output.interpretation: "Lung cancer" is too broad to analyse as it stands. The most likely reading is lung tumour tissue (case) vs adjacent non-cancerous lung tissue (control). Other possible comparisons include a specific subtype vs normal lung, drug-resistant vs parental cell lines, or treated vs untreated cells.

clarifying_questions.question: Which lung cancer type do you mean?
options: Non-small cell lung cancer, any type
clarifying_questions.why: The answer decides which series qualify. Two tumour-vs-normal tissue series I checked cover adenocarcinoma: GSE140343 (all adenocarcinoma) and GSE159857 (both subtypes). GSE159857 also covers squamous cell carcinoma, and GSE268175 is described as non-small cell lung cancer in general. The SCLC search found about 87 series, and the ones shown are almost all cell-line or xenograft experiments with no normal-lung control.

clarifying_questions.question: What should the comparison be?
options: Tumour vs adjacent normal lung tissue from patients
Drug-resistant vs parental cancer cell lines (e.g. resistance to osimertinib or KRAS G12C inhibitors)
Gene knockdown/knockout vs control in a lung cancer cell line
clarifying_questions.why: The non-small cell lung cancer search alone matched 197 series, mostly cell-line experiments, which is far more than the 10 the analysis can take. Each type of comparison leads to a different set of series.

clarifying_questions.question: Is there a gene, drug or pathway you are interested in?
clarifying_questions.why: This would narrow down the cell-line experiments, for example EGFR inhibitor resistance or KRAS G12C.
